messages:
Maya (Support): FYI — getting a handful of escalations: multiple customers hitting 502/503 and timeouts on /v1/generate in hosted. Started ~12:05. Tickets attached.

Maya (Support): Example customer log copy: 
`request_id=rl-9f3a timeout=20000ms status=502 error='gateway: upstream closed connection'`

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: release=2026-03-15-rc4 subset=15% targets=hosted-default (12:03 PST) :rocket:

Jordan (Oncall): I'm looking at edge logs now. Seeing a spike in "auth: key lookup failure" and 502s from gateway layer. Pulling traces.

Priya (Eng-runtime): Quick context — rc4 included a config flag flip in PR #5442: `auth.key_lookup_mode` changed from `RELAXED` -> `STRICT` to catch rotated keys. That flag was meant for Dedicated customers only.

Alex Chen (Eng-plat): ugh — flag targeting was wrong in the rollout manifest. It applied to hosted too. That will cause the gateway to reject requests where the rotated-key cache hasn't propagated, leading to 5xx and timeouts as proxy retries happen.

Samir Patel (SRE): Confirmed traces show majority of 5xx are from `auth-proxy: internal 500 on missing-key` then gateway translating to 502/503. Sample trace snippet:
```
auth-proxy ERROR: key_lookup failed: key_id not found (tenant=acct-779)
gateway WARN: upstream error -> translate 502
```

Maya (Support): Customers also reporting duplicate charge attempts because clients retried after timeouts. We have at least 4 support tickets flagged for billing.

support-bot: alert: spike detected on /v1/generate — 5xx rate 12% (baseline 0.4%) in us-west-2 (12:06 PST)

Alex Chen (Eng-plat): Rolling flag back now. Command: `infractl featureflag set auth.key_lookup_mode=RELAXED --scope=hosted --release=2026-03-15-rc4`

deploy-bot: Feature flag change applied to hosted (12:08 PST) — propagation starting across proxy fleet.

Samir Patel (SRE): After flag rollback, 5xx dropped in the canary group within ~40s: 12% -> 1.2%. Still seeing trailing errors due to edge cache TTL for rotated keys (10m).

Priya (Eng-runtime): To accelerate recovery: flush key lookup cache on edge nodes for hosted. Command we used: 
```
curl -X POST "https://edge-internal.us-west-2.redwood/v1/admin/cache/keys/flush" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
Run that against canary pool first, then full.

Jordan (Oncall): Flushed canary pool at 12:12. 5xx down to 0.3% in canary. Scheduling full flush now (12:14).

Maya (Support): Billing impact — customers say they got charged for retried requests. @Lina (Finance) can you freeze billing for affected tenants and prepare credits? I will attach request_ids.

Lina (Finance): On it. Need list of tenant IDs and associated request_id CSV. Please include time windows (12:03-12:18 PST). I'll coordinate credits and notify sales.

Alex Chen (Eng-plat): We'll produce the CSV. Action items: 1) Export request_id -> tenant -> billing events for 2026-03-15 12:00-12:20 PST. 2) Support to freeze billing on those tenants temporarily. 3) Prod change: ensure flag targeting cannot apply to hosted without explicit allowlist. 4) Add canary health checks to catch auth spikes pre-rollout.

Priya (Eng-runtime): Also creating a hotfix PR to change default behavior for `auth.key_lookup_mode` and add a pre-rollout validation script that checks flag scope mismatch.

Samir Patel (SRE): Post-incident steps: run a sweep to identify any other flags with global scope accidentally enabled in rc4. I'll run the audit script.

Maya (Support): Customer comms: I'll notify impacted customers that we identified a rollout flag mistake, reverted it, flushed caches, and that Finance will follow up about credits.

Jordan (Oncall): Incident classification: SEV3 (customer impact, partial degradation). Owner for postmortem: Priya. Timeline doc and RCA channel: #postmortems.

Maya (Support): Thanks team. Closing thread when billing credits are confirmed and postmortem is scheduled. :white_check_mark:
